findings.where: "Where we're starting" section: the Canggu, Uluwatu and Kuta Lombok cards, on desktop and phone
findings.fault: Each card has a thick 3px purple border. Purple is in none of the brand's colours and has no job on the page. The rules give cards a thin 1–1.5px sand-border edge. Next to the turquoise, ink, sand and coral, the purple boxes look like they came from another site, or like a selected or error state.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose rules say every colour has exactly one job and cards take sand-border. A visitor may also read the loud coloured edge as a state, such as selected or highlighted, that means nothing here.

findings.where: "Where we're starting" section: the three destination cards, on desktop and phone
findings.fault: The cards sit under a wide, heavy drop shadow even when nothing is happening. The rules say nothing sits at rest under a heavy shadow, and a shadow means 'you can act on this'. These cards are now deliberately static, but the shadow still makes them look like raised buttons, which goes against the fix pass 1 made to stop them looking clickable.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker on a phone taps a raised, shadowed card, expecting a guide, and nothing happens. The founder's rules also say borders come first and shadows are only for hover and popovers.

findings.where: "Where we're starting" section: the region labels (BALI, LOMBOK) and place names (Canggu, Uluwatu, Kuta Lombok) inside the cards, on desktop and phone
findings.fault: The card text is set in a monospace typewriter face that the page uses nowhere else, and that the brand doesn't have. Card titles should be Quicksand 600 and labels Nunito Sans. The region labels are also in capitals, which the rules keep for badges and filter labels. The cards read like code samples, not travel destinations, and clash with the rounded Quicksand heading right above them.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose type spec allows only Quicksand and Nunito Sans. A visitor gets a cold, technical feel on the one part of the page that names the places they'd go, the opposite of the beachy, effortless first feeling the brand wants.

findings.where: Hero: the coral "Email ... for launch news" button next to the "Explore destinations" outline button, on desktop and phone
findings.fault: The two hero buttons sit side by side but have different shapes. The coral one is a full pill, and the outline one has almost square corners. The rules give both buttons the same 8px control radius. They look like parts of two different systems rather than a main and a secondary action from one set.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose rules set 8px for controls and keep pills for badges, tags and status chips. A careful visitor sees the pair as mismatched, which makes the hero look unfinished.

findings.where: "Where we're starting" section heading, on desktop and phone
findings.fault: The section heading looks set at a lighter weight than the 600 the rules give h2 headings. Beside the bold hero headline it looks thin, so the page's two headings don't read as one family at two sizes.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose type spec sets h2 in Quicksand 600. A few careful visitors would notice the heading looking weaker than the rest of the type.
